author: Nina Moini and Ellen Finn
headline: Latino sexual assault survivor advocates grapple with César Chavez's legacy
news_topic: sexual-violence survivor advocacy; Operation Metro Surge; barriers to help seeking; community safety
collection_notes: MPR interviews Esperanza United's president/CEO. Although the immediate hook is César Chávez's legacy, the interview explicitly turns to Operation Metro Surge and reports the organization's observations that survivors were afraid to leave home, stay home, call for help, use hospitals, or engage police/courts; it closes with Esperanza United's bilingual 24/7 crisis line. Strong second-order affective-intermediation case within the final day of the study window.
